newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks drop at the open on Friday.
newsitem.headline: French stocks drop at the open on Friday.

text.p: French shares opened lower and dropped through technical support levels in early trading on Friday as worries about a rise in corporate tax and other deficit plugging measures weighed ahead of the release on Monday of an independent audit of public finances.
The market was also under technical pressure after reaching but failing to hold the key 3,000 level on Thursday, dealers said.

"The trend is toward profit taking while we wait to find out more on the tax increases to come," said a trader, who added that the world trading environment was still positive and that the rise in the dollar was limiting impulses to correct.
The blue chip CAC-40 index was down 42.17, or 1.43 percent at 2,916.42 0917 GMT. The July CAC-40 futures contract was at 2,918 vs 2,966 at Thursdays close.
Total volume was 930 million francs of which 780 million on the CAC-40.

A source close to the government said on Thursday that the government was studying raising corporate tax and increasing company social security contributions to help plug a budget deficit expected at around 3.6 percent of gross domestic product.
The market was also waiting for May U.S. trade figures to see what impact they might have on the dollar. The figures are due at 1230 GMT.
At 1400 GMT the University of Michigan July preliminary sentiment index will be released.

Club Mediteranee announced a first-half 1996/1997 net loss of 413 million francs after 630 million francs of charges. The company also warned of more charges in the second half, but said they would be lower than in the first six months.
The company said that in spite of the loss its financial situation remains healthy with financial debt limited to 2.4 billion francs for 3.5 billion francs shareholder's equity.
Former chairman Serge Trigano resigned from the company's surpervisory board over management style differences.
